extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, and their counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures used by the USPTO to decide whether to impose reciprocal discipline based on a final disciplinary adjudication by a state authority under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24. Covers the presumptions, respondent defenses, burdens, timing, and post-order obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final adjudication establishes prima facie case
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(e) '... a final adjudication in another jurisdiction ... or program that a practitioner ... has been guilty of misconduct shall establish a prima facie case by clear and convincing evidence that the practitioner violated 37 C.F.R. 10.23, as further identified under 37 C.F.R. 10.23(c)(5) ....' (citing Selling v. Radford).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A state disbarment creates a federal presumption that reciprocal discipline is proper absent successful defense under Selling; the USPTO treats a final state disciplinary adjudication as establishing the prima facie case for violation of USPTO ethical rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defenses permitting refusal of identical discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)(i)-(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall impose the identical discipline unless the practitioner clearly and convincingly demonstrates a genuine issue of material fact that: (i) the procedure elsewhere was so lacking in notice or opportunity to be heard as to constitute deprivation of due process; (ii) there was such infirmity of proof establishing the conduct as to give rise to the clear conviction that the Office could not, consistently with its duty, accept as final the conclusion on that subject; (iii) the imposition of the same discipline by the Office would result in grave injustice; or (iv) the practitioner was not the person disciplined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must raise one or more of these specific grounds and provide evidence creating a genuine issue of material fact to overcome the presumption of reciprocity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's burden of proof: clear and convincing evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal courts have generally concluded that in reciprocal discipline cases it is the respondent's burden to demonstrate, by clear and convincing evidence, that one of the Selling elements precludes reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard is high: the respondent must produce clear and convincing proof to establish lack of due process, infirmity of proof, grave injustice, or misidentification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due process deficiency standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A procedure is deficient if it was 'so lacking in notice or opportunity to be heard as to constitute a deprivation of due process.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To succeed on this ground the respondent must show the record demonstrates lack of notice or opportunity to be heard; mere disagreement with procedure or outcome is insufficient where the record shows notice and opportunities were provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infirmity of proof standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'infirmity of proof' exists only if there was such infirmity of proof establishing the conduct leading to the state discipline 'as to give rise to the clear conviction that the Office could not, consistently with its duty, accept as final the conclusion on that subject.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments about procedural defects (e.g., denied continuance) do not by themselves establish infirmity of proof. The respondent must show the evidence supporting the state finding was so deficient that the USPTO could not accept it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grave injustice standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline may be refused if 'the imposition of the same disciplinary sanction by the Office would result in grave injustice.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO evaluates asserted mitigating or extenuating circumstances (e.g., long prior good conduct, personal hardship, claimed mitigation) but requires clear and convincing evidence that applying the identical sanction would be unjust; speculative or unsupported assertions (e.g., potential bias without evidence) will not meet the standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity/misidentification challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: One permissible defense is that 'the practitioner was not the person disciplined as set forth' in the state judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the disciplined individual's identity is contested, the respondent must present convincing proof that the state proceedings apply to a different person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and contents of response to USPTO Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent was ordered to 'file, within forty (40) days of the date of the Notice and Order with the USPTO General Counsel, any response ... and file all information that Respondent believed sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact' under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A timely, substantive response is required: produce evidence and argument that create a genuine issue of material fact on one of the §11.24(d) grounds within the 40-day period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending state appeal does not automatically stay reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of an appeal 'does not, by itself justify a stay of reciprocal discipline proceedings or a finding of a genuine issue of material fact that imposition of disbarment would result in a grave injustice.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents cannot avoid or indefinitely delay reciprocal discipline simply by filing an appeal in the state forum; USPTO may proceed unless clear reasons for a stay are shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: State evidence rules and exclusions may bear on USPTO review
rubrics_metrics.description: State rules of evidence (e.g., Texas Rules of Evidence: Dead Man's Rule, hearsay rules, Statute of Frauds, Rule 1004, Rule 803(3)) and their application in the state proceeding can be addressed by respondent as part of alleging infirmity of proof or due process problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO will consider whether exclusions under state evidence rules were reasonable; absence of admissible evidence due to valid state-law evidentiary rulings does not necessarily establish infirmity of proof unless it causes an unfair outcome under federal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orders and practitioner obligations upon exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: If exclusion is ordered: (a) Respondent is excluded from practice before the Office; (b) Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office for 30 days to wind up client business; (c) Respondent must withdraw from employment in pending proceedings in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 10040 (as directed); (d) Respondent must not accept new clients before the Office during the limited recognition period; (e) Respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60 upon discipline and any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order imposes concrete obligations and time-limited wind-up authority; compliance with specific C.F.R. provisions (publication, notice, reinstatement procedures, and client-windup/withdrawal rules) is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements following discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order and publish a Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette; the OED Director shall give notice of public discipline and the reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary results are publicly posted and notified to relevant state and court authorities; respondents should expect public disclosure and inter-agency notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of state appellate affirmance for USPTO purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: A state Board of Disciplinary Appeals' 'Judgment Affirming Judgment of Disbarment' is deemed a final adjudication in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(e), which supports the prima facie case for reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the state appellate body affirms disbarment and the judgment is final, the USPTO's presumption of reciprocity is triggered absent successful clear-and-convincing proof of a §11.24(d) defense.
